results.title: Is this an Amazon recruiting scam?
results.snippet: The clearest warning sign is any request to pay money upfront. Scammers may claim you need to buy a laptop, software, training materials, background-check services, work-from-home equipment, or gift cards before starting. Some send a fake check and ask you to deposit it, buy equipment from a specific “vendor,” and return leftover funds. results.title: Is this Amazon work-from-home job real? | Real Job Check
results.snippet:
Amazon is a real company, and it does hire for remote roles, which is exactly why scammers impersonate it so often. A message about an Amazon work-from-home or data-entry job is probably fake if it asks you to pay for equipment, asks for bank or Social Security details up front, or moves you to WhatsApp or Telegram. Amazon's real openings are on its own jobs site, never in an unsolicited text.
